character_facts: Don Nicanor commands Philodendran forces and does not remember Dona Vicenta is his daughter during this recap.
Dona Vicenta is capable of extreme bodily sacrifice and later pleads for her people.
Melmoth reacts with horror to Dona Vicenta's altered eyes.
Steelhead is presented as one facet of Melmoth and favors action or hardness.
Zaran is presented as the poet side of Melmoth and responds with revulsion and despair.
Tonto and Lothar survive the destruction of the Metabunker and start constructing another one.
continuity_links: This page is explicitly a recap of events from earlier chapters in The Metabarons.
The page sets up the frame narrative involving Tonto and Lothar telling Metabaron history after the Metabunker's destruction.
The recap ties together the family conflict around Dona Vicenta and Melmoth with the larger planetary conflict involving the Techno-Technos.
dialogue_meaning: The recap explains prior events rather than presenting active scene dialogue.

lore_facts: The Metabunker can be destroyed and rebuilt.
Tonto and Lothar act as narrators or custodians of Metabaron history while stranded.
Dona Vicenta has cybernetic eyes by this point in the story.
Melmoth's psyche is divided into Steelhead and Zaran.
The Techno-Technos seek to harvest a mineral called Bikramen.
A TechnoCardinal serves as a representative or authority figure for the Techno-Technos.
The invading force attacks by dropping huge rectangular blocks onto the planet.
plot_events: The Metabaron destroys the Metabunker, leaving Tonto and Lothar stranded on a muddy, primitive world.
Tonto and Lothar begin building a new Metabunker and continue recounting Metabaron history.
Don Nicanor and his Philodendran forces break into the place where Melmoth and Dona Vicenta are barricaded.
Don Nicanor tries to claim Dona Vicenta without recognizing she is his daughter.
Dona Vicenta asks what feature he values most in her, and after he answers, she removes her fingernails and gives them to him.
Don Nicanor, tormented by this, permits her marriage to Melmoth and grants a high-status decoration.
Melmoth is horrified by his wife's new cybernetic eyes, and his split personality fractures again into its two parts.
One side of Melmoth, Steelhead, approves of the new eyes, while the poet side, Zaran, is disgusted.
A TechnoCardinal tells Don Nicanor that his people must leave their planet so the Techno-Technos can mine Bikramen.
Don Nicanor refuses, and the Techno-Technos begin bombarding the planet with massive rectangular blocks.
Don Nicanor's forces cannot resist the invaders' weapons.
Dona Vicenta begs Steelhead to fight for her people, but Zaran sees no future for them.
Steelhead kills himself to remove the poet side from the situation.

visual_summary: An introductory recap page for The Metabarons. The page features the series logo, a large 'previously' summary block, a painted inset image of a dark figure amid violent debris, and a decorative biomechanical border with small circular character portraits along the bottom. Credits and publisher information fill the lower margin.
